title: Piano and drum house parties and Frazier pianists
summary: Piano and drum jobs at lawn parties were plentiful; Jiles worked with Mitchell and Simon Frazier and a pianist called Herman.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What about, did they have many jobs for just piano or piano and drums and those things?
Oh they had lots of piano and drums, because they had a lot of house parties, what they would call lawn parties. That was practically, they had more jobs than the bands did, piano and drums.
Did you work many of them?
Oh yeah, that was my biggest start. And you know, piano and drummers, house parties, it was great.
Who was it that you were with? What piano played?
Mitchell Frazier, you heard talk of him.
Is that Saean's brother or not?
Mitchell Frazier, that's his cousin. What did he play?
Oh he's old Dixieland, great piano. Now I played with Simon Frazier too now, that's Saean's brother. Yeah. Mitchell is the cousin and Simon is Saean's brother.
They weren't just one number man, they could play Dixieland? Dixieland.

All the Dixieland. Piano players, facts would make them famous, they would get the numbers quicker than the bands would. It was great at that time. There was a lot of work for piano players and drummers.
Did you play with piano players before you played with bands?
No, but I played more often, more jobs. I played with the bands, boys. But I played more often.
Let's see now those piano players, like that, wasn't that guy called Herman or something you had on the tape?

That's right, Herman. I played with him, well I played with him concerts and dances, but I was with a band with him, with Bill Hamilton and Lawrence Toka and Melvin Frank and Eddie Summers. What was Herman's name? I can't recall his name, because they used to call him Skeet, but his name was Herman, but I want to recall his name. What about Buddy Petit?
